items.text: You can now sign in with just your email — we send a six-digit code, so there's no password to set or forget. Google sign-in still works as before.

A free account now includes one personalized league. Import it from Sleeper, Yahoo or ESPN — or enter your scoring by hand — and your board is re-scored for your actual settings, with value over replacement computed against your real starting lineup. My League leads with what changed in your scoring, and why.

The NFL fantasy rankings and projections are now free to read, with every number real — our projection, rank, 80% range and market ADP for every player, no account needed. The free board is full-PPR, twelve-team; other formats and league sizes are part of a membership.

Rankings and the League Board now show how far each player has moved from our generic board once you select your own league — the "vs our generic board" comparison that used to live only on My League.

A "full-season rate" column now sits beside expected points on the rankings, projections and player pages — what a player is worth in the weeks he plays, stretched over a full 17 games, so two players with different injury risk are easier to compare.

Our projected points are now labelled "Expected pts" everywhere. They already price in the games we expect a player to miss, so they run lower than an "if he plays every week" number — the Track Record shows projected games beside them so you can see the discount. Point rankings are unchanged.
The membership page now shows the price, billing period and remaining founding-member seats before you sign up — read straight from Stripe, so what's advertised is what's billed.
You can now create an account yourself — one click with Google, or with your email. Signing up is free, you subscribe when you want to, and you land back on whatever page you started from.
Player Search no longer requires an account, and a retired player's page now shows his past seasons instead of "player not found".
On a phone, the menu no longer runs off the bottom of the screen — Sign Out and Settings are always reachable, and it scrolls on its own without moving the page behind it.

A new My Teams page (NFL → Fantasy) shows every league you've imported in one place, each roster scored under that league's own format. Tell us which team is yours and your starters and bench show up with a season projection and 80% range. Per-game splits and waivers arrive with the weekly model.

Opened three NFL fantasy pages under NFL → Fantasy — Projections, Rankings and the League Board. Every player's 2026 projection is re-scored for your league's format and size, with an 80% range on every number and value over replacement on the board.

Kickers and defenses (K and D/ST) are now projected, and your league's exact scoring applies precisely — field goals by distance, the points-allowed tier table, and yards-allowed tiers — because we emit raw components rather than a single total. These are the least predictable positions, so read them as a streaming tier with wide ranges, not a precise rank.

Every player now has his own page — full projected stat line, fantasy points under standard, half-PPR, full-PPR and your own league, his 80% range drawn as a band, position rank, value over replacement, tier, and where the market is drafting him. Reach it from any board or from Player Search.

Player pages gained a headshot and bio, a breakdown of what pushes each player's number up or down (in actual points, from a separate research model — a second independent read, not a receipt for the projection), and a subscriber History panel: how he finished each season back to 2019, that year's ADP, a weekly injury log, and a plain-language consistency read.

Added market ADP to the Rankings and League Board, with a "vs ADP" column showing where our board and the public disagree — matched to your scoring format and league size. It's a reference point, not a claim our order is the better one.
The boards gained value tiers (a break where there's an unusually large drop to the next player), named replacement-level players, pagination, and clearer self-explaining column labels.

Players who sat out all of last season (Brandon Aiyuk, Tank Dell) are back on the board — projected off their most recent season played, with a hard availability discount and a Low-confidence badge, so they usually sit below where the market drafts them.

We recalibrated our 80% projection ranges against what players actually did. The old method under-covered badly — only ~55% of veterans finished inside their range — so ranges are now read from comparable players' real outcomes, position by position, and are honestly wider (a late-round veteran's floor is often zero). Point projections are unchanged.

Pick email alerts now arrive as lineups confirm through the day, when your lineup-confirmed picks are ready — instead of a single morning email built on preliminary picks. Moneyline and totals only, each pick emailed once.

Fixed a scoring bug where ESPN-imported leagues ignored passing, rushing and receiving yards — the bulk of fantasy scoring — so those boards had been ranking almost entirely on touchdowns and receptions. Every ESPN league is now corrected with no re-import needed. Sleeper and Yahoo were never affected.

Fixed player pages showing an IL badge on healthy, playing players — 62 of the 187 flagged as injured had already played since. Status now clears whenever a player appears in a game, and is checked daily against that exact contradiction.

The MLB prospect board now shows a traded prospect's current organization and puts him on the right AL/NL sheet — org comes from MLB's own data instead of FanGraphs' editorial board, which doesn't repoint a player when he's traded.
The Settings page now tells you the truth about a canceled subscription — the exact date your access continues through, instead of still showing "Active subscription".

Bets on late games at the end of a month no longer sit "Pending" forever. We now ask MLB directly for a final when our own records don't show one, and alert ourselves if any bet stays pending more than a day after first pitch.
Strikeout prop bets in the Bet Log now settle the same night the game ends, graded from MLB's official box score, instead of waiting a day for our pitch-tracking data to rebuild.

We briefly swapped the model behind our projected run totals on August 2nd and reverted it the same day — re-scoring both showed the original was better calibrated, so we put it back. Neither model's per-game uncertainty is where we want it yet; that's what we're working on. Totals bets remain paused, and this was never a betting claim.

Added a "Predictive distribution" section to the totals pick-detail page — the model's full calibrated view of how a game's scoring could land: the game-total distribution with the market line drawn on it, an 80% range, the probability of the over, and per-team and alternate-line ladders. It's a transparency view of the model's uncertainty, not a bet recommendation.

Added two-factor authentication (Settings → Two-Factor Authentication) — turn on an authenticator app and enter a 6-digit code alongside your password each sign-in. If you sign in with Google, 2FA is already handled by your Google account.
Added "Continue with Google" to the sign-in page — sign in in one tap instead of typing an email and password. Credence never sees your Google password.

Win rate, record and ROI now mean exactly the same thing everywhere — win rate excludes pushes, records count one call per market, and ROI is your result net of the book's cut. Rates from only a handful of bets carry a plain "small sample" caveat, and the number of bets behind a rate is shown beside it.

A Parlay Calculator is here (Betting → Parlay Calculator). Build a parlay from the day's slate and see our model's true combined probability next to the price the book implies, plus expected value per dollar and a plain verdict. Same-game legs are correlation-adjusted rather than naively multiplied. Most parlays are negative expected value once the vig is priced in, and this is built to show you that.

You can now log a strikeout prop into your Bet Log — copied from a pitcher's projection, or back-logged for one you already placed — and it settles automatically against his actual strikeouts once the game is final.

Bet alerts (Settings → Notifications) — opt in to be told by email or browser push when the model posts qualified plays for the day. Most days nothing fires. These are model outputs, not betting advice.
Completed games now show a "who called it" scorecard — which side the model favored on the moneyline and total, and whether the call was right, shown as plainly for a miss as for a hit.

A new Props page (Betting dropdown) shows every probable starter's projected strikeout total for the day, with the book's posted line and the model-minus-book gap, sorted highest first. Click any card for the full distribution and per-book breakdown.

Starting pitcher pages now show our projected strikeout total for their next start, next to the book's line, with a per-book de-vigged Over% comparison. Single-game strikeout totals are high-variance — treat it as context, not a play.

The Performance page now shows a Bankroll by Sportsbook breakdown — balance, net deposits, betting P&L and growth per book. Growth is return on deposited funds, kept distinct from ROI (return on stake).

Each pick's detail page now shows a Line Movement chart across all seven books — how the moneyline and total drifted from open to current, with a de-vigged Over% view for totals. A market-context view, not an edge claim.

Matchup heatmaps are live on pick and player pages — a strike-zone heatmap of where a batter does damage, overlaid with where the pitcher actually locates each pitch type, with pitch-type toggles and per-cell detail. A show-your-work matchup view; the zone signal tested null for predictive edge.

Line Shopping on the EV Tracker — model-positive plays ranked by edge, with the best available US price and the book offering it highlighted per play, plus Pinnacle's fair-value anchor. On each pick, the best-priced book is marked with a "BEST" badge.
Settings now has a Sportsbooks section — add each book you use, set its balance, and record deposits and withdrawals, so bankroll growth reflects only betting results, not cash movement.

Book Comparison now shows a model breakeven price per pick — the price at which the model's edge reaches zero — alongside Pinnacle's no-vig fair value, and each book's hold (vig), with the tightest book flagged (Pinnacle ~2%, US books 4–8%).

The models behind the picks are now leak-free. The old ones over-credited a bullpen metric that was partly computed from the game being predicted; the new ones remove that and are far leaner, so the displayed "why this pick" drivers now reflect what the model actually weighs. Picks and probabilities may shift.

Win probabilities are now calibrated to be honest about how close most MLB games are — numbers shown near 75–85% were really closer to a coin flip. When we say 55%, the home team wins about 55%. Treat every pick as a lean, not a lock.

A Book Comparison panel on every game-detail page — pick a book and see its moneyline and totals prices alongside the model's probability, the book's de-vigged market %, and expected value per dollar, with Pinnacle as the sharp low-vig anchor.
Pick pages now show a model conviction score and an 80% win-probability range for moneyline picks — a confidence signal, showing how wide the model's uncertainty is, not a recommendation to bet.

A Teams directory (/teams) — all 30 MLB teams by division with record, win %, and streak — plus team pages with ELO trend, platoon splits, recent form, upcoming schedule with probable starters, and key stats.
A Players directory (/players) — searchable batter and pitcher lists with core stats, each linking through to a full player profile.
Pick pages now show model reasoning — a plain-English narrative plus signed feature drivers grouped by category (starting pitcher, bullpen, team offense, park & weather).
Blog posts are now public at /blog, with the latest surfaced on the home page.
FAQ and Contact pages published, covering model methodology, platform mechanics and responsible use.
